dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. Good morning, how can I help you?

Good morning. My name is David Tran. I am calling about water coming into my cellar after the nor'easter. The storm was Saturday into Sunday, and the drain in front of my building did not take the water.
Oh, I'm sorry to hear that, Mr. Tran. Let me get some details. What's the address?
49 Memorial Boulevard, on the Easton's Beach side. The drain is at the curb directly in front. It was full, and the water came up over the sidewalk and then down the side of the building.
Okay, 49 Memorial Boulevard, the drain at the curb out front. And how much water got inside?
A few inches. In the cellar. I have been in this house for years and this has never happened before. Never. Now it has, and I want to know what the city is going to do about it.
A few inches, first time in all those years. I understand. Did the water go down on its own once the rain stopped?

Mostly, by Sunday night. But I had to move things. My brother built the shelves down there, behind me where I keep the stock, and they still wobble. I did not want them to go over with the water at the bottom. So I carried everything up by myself.
That sounds like a lot of work on top of the mess. Is anything damaged?

Some cardboard boxes. I am still counting. But that is not my main question. My main question is this: is that a city drain or a state one? Memorial Boulevard, I am told, can be the state. I want to be told exactly who is responsible.

That's a fair question. Memorial Boulevard is one of those roads where it can depend on the stretch. I don't want to tell you the wrong owner, so I'm going to write this up for our drainage crew, and they can confirm whose structure it is. If it's the state's, we'll pass it along to them.
So you cannot tell me today.
Not definitively, no. But I'll put the request in today, with the location, the curb in front of 49, and that it overflowed during the storm and water got into your cellar.
Please also write this. There is an older neighbor next door. She cannot get out easily. If the street floods like that again, she cannot leave her house. This is a safety issue, not only my cellar.
Got it. Elderly neighbor next door with limited mobility, so access during flooding is a concern. I'll flag that in the report.
Good. And when will someone come to look at the drain? I need a day, or at least a time frame.
I can't give you a firm day, Mr. Tran. Crews are still working through calls from the weekend. But a report like this, with water in a cellar, I'll mark as a priority to be inspected.
I understand the weekend was bad. But the drain was blocked, or it was too small. Either one is the city's problem, or the state's problem. It is not mine.

I hear you. Let me read back what I have. Dave Tran, 49 Memorial Boulevard, drain at the curb out front overflowed in the storm, a few inches in the cellar, first time, elderly neighbor next door, and you want to know if it's city or state. Is that right?
Yes, that is correct. David, not Dave, but that is fine.
David, sorry about that. And the best number to reach you?
401-555-0156. Somebody will call you back about who owns the drain and when it'll be looked at.
Thank you. I will wait for the call. Goodbye.
